title: Enrollment Analysis: Non-Hispanic Black students comprised 3.7% of Sandusky County's student body in 2023-24 school year
text:
Paul Craft Ohio Superintendent of Public Instruction | https://www.linkedin.com/in/paul-craft-5b033a4a/
Paul Craft Ohio Superintendent of Public Instruction | https://www.linkedin.com/in/paul-craft-5b033a4a/
Ohio Department of Education & Workforce.
Data showed that Sandusky County welcomed 7,900 students during the 2023-24 school year. Among them, non-Hispanic Black students comprised 3.7% of the student body to be the least represented ethnicity in the county.
Among the 19 schools in Sandusky County, Fremont Ross High School recorded the highest enrollment of non-Hispanic Black students in the 2023-24 school year, with a total of 74 students.
In 2022, Ohio saw an
average student-to-teacher ratio of approximately 1:15, which is an improvement for the state and is lower than the national average of 1:16.
Despite the apparent improvement, this positive trend is overshadowed by a general decline in public school enrollments, which was accelerated by the pandemic. This decline, aligned with the steady number of teachers in the state over the last 10 years, has led to low student-to-teacher ratios.
